classification.classification_note: ASan labels the fault as a std::vector container-overflow read. Semantically, the bug is an out-of-bounds read caused by inconsistent channel/meta-channel bookkeeping in bundled libjxl.

bug_description.normalized: The staged 235-byte witness is accepted as a JPEG XL image and reaches `jxl::ModularDecode()` while decoding global modular info. `Bundle::Read(br, &header)` materializes a transform list that, on the witnessed path, applies a palette transform before a squeeze transform with no explicit squeeze parameters. Vulnerable `MetaPalette()` unconditionally increments `input.nb_meta_channels` and reshapes `input.channel`, which can leave the meta-channel count inconsistent with the post-palette channel vector. When the later squeeze transform reaches `MetaSqueeze()`, `parameters->empty()` is true so `DefaultSqueezeParameters()` derives its defaults from that inconsistent state. It then dereferences `image.channel[image.nb_meta_channels]` as the first non-meta channel, and AddressSanitizer reports `container-overflow READ 8` at `lib/jxl/modular/transform/squeeze.cc:145`.

source.description: First project-side parse of the attacker-controlled modular transform bundle that drives the vulnerable path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` file is a 235-byte JPEG XL witness processed through `JxlDecoderProcessInput()`. In `ModularFrameDecoder::DecodeGlobalInfo()`, its global modular bitstream is passed to `ModularDecode()` as `BitReader *br`, and this call materializes the transform list from those bytes.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. Default squeeze derivation uses `image.nb_meta_channels` as the first non-meta channel index without first proving that the index is within the logical `image.channel` vector.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: container-overflow` with `READ of size 8` at `lib/jxl/modular/transform/squeeze.cc:145:52` in `jxl::DefaultSqueezeParameters`.

root_cause.description: Vulnerable palette meta-apply unconditionally assumes the transform adds exactly one meta channel. For attacker-selected transform contexts where that assumption is false, `nb_meta_channels` no longer matches the logical first non-meta channel after the palette reshapes `input.channel`.
root_cause.note: The saved artifacts do not recover the exact `begin_c`/`num_c` values, but the earlier `MetaPalette` allocation context proves this bookkeeping update ran before the crashing default squeeze read.

tainted_value_origin.description: This read materializes the vulnerability-relevant transform state from attacker bytes: the same transform list later applies a palette transform and then a squeeze transform with an empty `squeezes` vector, which forces default squeeze parameter derivation.

parser_admitted.description: After the outer JPEG XL parser accepts the witness, libjxl hands the global modular stream to `ModularGenericDecompress()`, which immediately descends into `ModularDecode()` and the vulnerable transform meta-apply path.
parser_admitted.condition: The saved ASan stack includes `jxl::ModularFrameDecoder::DecodeGlobalInfo -> jxl::ModularGenericDecompress -> jxl::ModularDecode` before the crashing transform frames.

coarse_trace.summary: JPEG XL global modular decoding is entered for the witness and dispatches the attacker-controlled bitstream into `ModularGenericDecompress()`.
`ModularDecode()` parses the transform bundle from the bitstream and applies the transforms sequentially to the in-memory `image` description.
An earlier palette transform from that list reshapes `image.channel` and updates `image.nb_meta_channels`; ASan's allocation context for the later crash points to this vector mutation.
A later squeeze transform has no explicit squeeze parameters, so `MetaSqueeze()` falls back to `DefaultSqueezeParameters()` and derives channel ranges from the already-mutated image state.
Default squeeze derivation trusts the inconsistent `image.nb_meta_channels` value as a channel index and performs the out-of-bounds vector read reported by ASan.

fine_trace.note: Source. Parses the attacker-controlled modular transform bundle from the bitstream into `header.transforms`. The saved crash and allocation stacks prove this parsed list later reaches an earlier palette transform and then a squeeze transform with an empty `squeezes` vector.

fine_trace.code:
return MetaPalette(input, begin_c, begin_c + num_c - 1, nb_colors,
                   nb_deltas, lossy_palette);
fine_trace.note: While `ModularDecode()` iterates the parsed transform list, an earlier transform with `id == TransformId::kPalette` reaches the palette branch and invokes `MetaPalette()` on attacker-selected channel parameters. In the vulnerable revision this path relies on `CheckEqualChannels()` only for raw range/dimension checks, so no guard here revalidates whether the selected range is compatible with the current meta/non-meta bookkeeping before step 3 updates it.

Root cause. `MetaPalette()` unconditionally increments `input.nb_meta_channels` as though the palette always consumes non-meta channels. On the witnessed path that assumption is unsafe, so the counter no longer reliably names the first non-meta channel after the vector rewrite in step 4.

Using the bookkeeping from step 3, `MetaPalette()` removes part of the existing channel range and inserts the palette table channel at the front of the vector. ASan's allocation stack points to this `insert()` as the allocation site of the `std::vector<Channel>` storage later read past its logical end.

Later in the same transform loop, a parsed squeeze transform reaches `MetaSqueeze()` with no explicit `SqueezeParams`. Because `parameters->empty()` is true, the code must derive default squeeze ranges from the current `image` state left by the earlier palette application.

Default squeeze derivation interprets `image.nb_meta_channels` as the count of meta channels and subtracts it from the current vector size to infer how many ordinary image channels remain. Because steps 3 and 4 may already have desynchronized that counter from the actual vector layout, this arithmetic no longer safely identifies the accessible non-meta portion of `image.channel`.

Sink. The code immediately dereferences `image.channel[image.nb_meta_channels]` as the first non-meta channel with no guard that `image.nb_meta_channels < image.channel.size()`. On the witnessed path that index falls into the vector's poisoned container tail, producing ASan's `container-overflow READ 8` at this exact line.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context points to the same `MetaPalette()` vector rewrite recorded in fine-trace step 4. Step 3's unconditional `input.nb_meta_channels++` is the bookkeeping update in that same function that makes the later squeeze default indexing unsafe.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: The saved ASan crash stack directly covers fine-trace steps 5-7 (`MetaSqueeze -> Transform::MetaApply -> ModularDecode`) and the allocation stack grounds step 4 in `MetaPalette()`. The staged artifacts do not recover the exact parsed `begin_c`, `num_c`, or full preceding transform history beyond the observed palette-before-squeeze ordering.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The transform descriptors parsed in step 1 select the earlier palette application in step 2 and the later empty-parameter squeeze in step 5; the inconsistent `nb_meta_channels` state from steps 3-4 is then used as the sink index in step 7.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged `libvips` merge diff does not expose a direct hunk in bundled `lib/jxl/...`, so Stage 02 does not claim fixed-version resolution from patch text alone.

format.name: JPEG XL codestream
format.contract: The file must remain a JPEG XL input that reaches global modular decoding with a transform list that applies a palette transform before a squeeze transform with `num_squeezes == 0`, so `DefaultSqueezeParameters()` derives defaults from the palette-mutated channel state.
